guardianfootball.title: Fifa’s World Cup TV rights documents indicate hydration breaks will stay in 2030
guardianfootball.description: Controversial breaks were financial boon for broadcasters Fifa flags possible benefits but says no decision made Fifa’s tender documents for TV rights for the 2030 World Cup includes a provision for broadcasters to sell adverts during hydration breaks in a strong indication the controversial stoppages will be retained. A three-minute break midway through each half was introduced for the first time at all 104 matches at last summer’s World Cup in the interests of player welfare, a radical move that also provided a commercial boon for broadcasters, particularly the rights holders in the United States, Fox Sports and Telemundo. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.description: Everton forward has magical talent and popularity to burn, but has come up against hard reality of the modern game Thomas Tuchel has never called up the player he once claimed to love “everything about”. The reason for Jack Grealish’s omission from Tuchel’s first England squad in March 2025 was given as “he simply has no rhythm”. Catch a falling star? Grealish was suspended by Everton for three matches following “a breach of club discipline”. Suggestions his loan from Manchester City might be cancelled were calmed by David Moyes. Last week, Grealish played in a behind-closed doors friendly against Derby before issuing an Instagram statement: “I want to apologise to the fans and everyone at…

guardianfootball.title: Overlap, underlap or sit back? How Premier League teams use their full-backs
guardianfootball.description: The role of full-back has changed massively in recent years. We analyse how all 20 sides are approaching the position By Opta Analyst Overlapping. Underlapping. Inverted. Traditional. The role of full-back has evolved dramatically. Once a defensive-first position that provided some auxiliary attacking support, the role has developed into something far more multifaceted. Just ask right-back Ben White, who – with Riccardo Calafiori on the left – has been an important figure in Arsenal’s superb start to the campaign. Talking a few years ago, he said: “Playing full-back the way [Mikel Arteta] wants is completely different to any other manager. To play full-back for him, you’ve got to be a…

guardianfootball.title: Swing when you’re winning? Biggest leaps across Fifa’s football rankings | The Knowledge
guardianfootball.description: Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more Mail us with all of your questions and answers “The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,” writes Bogdan Kotarlic. “Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team?” The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles. And, as Chris Lewis and others point out, there are a couple of other home nations who have had…

guardianfootball.title: ‘The game is in danger’: PFA head Maheta Molango on Fifa, Infantino and football’s future
guardianfootball.description: At a potentially critical juncture for football, the PFA chief executive talks about the organisation, wider fears in the game and why the Folarin Balogun affair was ‘scandalous’ After five years in charge of the Professional Footballers’ Association, what has Maheta Molango learned? “The game is in danger,” the 43-year-old says. “I’ve learned that the game I loved and led me to first play and then advise and then lead a club and today to lead the PFA, is in danger because it is being forgotten.” In 2026, with football ubiquitous on all platforms, with a World Cup that generated $15bn (£11.4m) in revenue, and with attendances across the English pyramid growing year on year, it may seem…

guardianfootball.title: Nations League roundup: Devenny’s divine strike lifts Northern Ireland to top tier
guardianfootball.description: Haaland’s late penalty grabs Norway last-eight spot Parrott penalties help Republic of Ireland secure playoff A wonder strike from Justin Devenny earned Northern Ireland top spot in Nations League Group B2 and promotion to the top tier of the competition. The Stoke player fired home on the volley from the edge of the area to earn a 1-1 draw away to Hungary , who would have leapfrogged Michael O’Neill’s side in the group with victory. Northern Ireland had fallen 1-0 behind after a 35th-minute goal from the striker Barnabas Varga, who slotted home when one-on-one with the goalkeeper Pierce Charles after a defensive mix-up. The goal ended Northern Ireland’s proud record of not having conceded…

guardianfootball.title: Portugal’s new No 7 Forbs channels Ronaldo for winner as Wales are denied
guardianfootball.description: One way or another, Portugal’s No 7 shirt has caused quite the commotion in recent weeks and months, if not years. Perhaps it was inevitable, then, that the first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era would come courtesy of the player wearing the updated jersey, one with a cross through the number to preserve Ronaldo’s eternal legacy, as the Portuguese Football Federation put it. A sumptuous finish by Carlos Forbs, a second-half substitute, was ultimately enough to clinch victory on a topsy-turvy night with Portugal surviving Pedro Neto’s sending-off for two yellow cards. For Wales, a Nations League relegation playoff double-header awaits in March, with Slovenia, Hungary, Republic of…

guardianfootball.title: Wayne Rooney says he contemplated taking own life during playing career
guardianfootball.description: Former England footballer opens up on mental health ‘It was probably the lowest point’ at Manchester United Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated taking his own life. The former England striker said that, even as he flourished on the pitch, he was struggling with his mental health off it, despite being newly married and a dad to his eldest child, Kai. He said he would spend two days at a time drinking at home and, he told the Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, at his lowest point considered taking his own life. Continue reading...

pitchfork.description: The Toronto singer caps her breakout year with a deluxe edition of her debut, a potent blend of 2010s R&B glam, sticky synth-pop, and heroic self-hype.

pitchfork.description: On his sixth album, Jade Lilitri reckons with a crowded mind, a shortened attention span, and the dream of better days ahead in a set of jittery emo and power-pop songs.

pitchfork.title: Beginningless
pitchfork.description: A group with ties to SML and Jeff Parker’s ETA IVtet puts an atmospheric spin on the classic bass/drums/horn trio format, using subtle electronic detailing to play up the music’s shifting textures.

pitchfork.title: 40 Acres
pitchfork.description: The DMV-based rapper spotlights his community and his loose, nonchalant flow on a breezy new project, executive-produced by MIKE and Surf Gang’s Elipropperr.

pitchfork.description: A sense of creepy unease permeates the Ohio noise veteran’s latest album, in which funny ha-ha is never far from funny uh-oh.

pitchfork.description: On its first album, the Canadian quartet hones its apocalyptic sludgegaze to reflect our unforgiving world and the psychological turmoil it foments.

pitchfork.title: file_1
pitchfork.description: Inspired by the video games and grime music he grew up on, the 24-year-old English rapper applies the hard-hitting flows to songs full of bright synths and heavy emotions.

quietus.title: The Strange World Of… The New Blockaders
quietus.description: Nick Soulsby, author of a new book charting TNB's bizarre 45-year journey, selects ten points of entry into the maze-like discography of a group dedicated to absurdity and the refusal of fixed meaning TNB at Cafe Oto in 2017, by Baby RL At the tail-end of the 70s, artists in the non-academic realm joined illustrious composers of electroacoustic and experimental music in probing where the outer limits of music might lie, and the extent to which its core characteristics could be twisted to unleash new sounds. Magnetic tape and fanzine culture alike inspired a wider web of individuals with no industry-backing, no money, no audience, and no media connections to create, then to share their work…

quietus.title: Brassica Unbound: Serge Gainsbourg’s L’Homme à tête de chou at 50
quietus.description: In 1976 the dandyish Gainsbourg embraced prog rock on a concept album about a man with a cabbage for a head but, says Jeremy Allen, he was still revered by French punks In 1975, Serge Gainsbourg was caught between a rock and a hard place. His solo career was fading steadily, with albums like Histoire de Melody Nelson and Vu de l'extérieur commercially underperforming in France. His English lover Jane Birkin, meanwhile, was enjoying A-list celebrity status with hit films such as Claude Zidi's La course à l'échalote. This reversal in their celebrity statuses aroused a streak of jealousy in him that would manifest itself in conceptual violence via his next album L'Homme à tête de chou,…

quietus.title: Anthony Child – Beginning of the Shadow
quietus.description: Anthony Child Beginning of the Shadow The Northamptonshire-born producer, aka Surgeon, purges himself in Maui with a suite of ten ambient explorations Beginning of the Shadow by Anthony Child Transcendence Orchestra, a duo featuring Anthony Child and Dan Bean, played at the Hottest Supernormal Festival Ever™ in 2022. Clad in chunky hooded robes, they took to a Vortex stage doing its best sweat-box-inside-a-greenhouse-inside-a-volcano impression and still managed to entrance a crowd sporting skimpy jorts and sweat dipped vests who could hardly hack the heat. The pair showed a thing or two about patience that day. About withstanding great physical discomfort. Some might even call it…

quietus.title: A Man Without a Soul: The The’s Infected at 40
quietus.description: Infected represented many things, says Wesley Doyle, one of them being how the cult artist Matt Johnson convinced a major label to bankroll a film, and what the ultimate cost of this was Imagine the scenario: it’s 1986 and a relatively unknown artist’s manager approaches his record label to finagle enough money to make a film to promote a new album. The sum they have in mind is around £500,000 – the best part of £2 million in today’s money. Eventually, the label capitulates, and the artist is flown around the world with several video directors and crew to make short films to accompany every track on the record. Even today, such an undertaking would only be possible for an artist of...

quietus.title: Feedbacker: Rock Music for November by JR Moores
quietus.description: Before rounding up some new rock releases – including a rancid new offering from "false redneck" Kid Rock – JR Moores praises the veteran Queen drummer, Roger Taylor Clutter, photo by Dan Kendall I realise this space would be better used to champion the kind of upcomin’, geetar abusin’, consensus challengin’, taboo bustin’ insurrectionists that would make Lambrini Girls look like Amanda Holden. Nevertheless, here are some thoughts on the white-bearded multimillionaire who wrote ‘Radio Ga Ga’. Frankly I’ve become so beguiled by the recent record from Queen’s drummer, I owe it to our readers to put it on their radar in case they’ve missed it, in all its uninhibited glory.I can’t say I’m au…

quietus.title: Iceboy Violet – How to Glitch Under The Map
quietus.description: Iceboy Violet How to Glitch Under The Map New album from the Manchester-based producer rides high on raw emotion How To Glitch Under The Map by Iceboy Violet In Jane Schoenbrun’s movies, I Saw The TV Glow and Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma, virtual and real bleed into each other as adults become threaded with their teenage obsessions, in the case of the former a spooky TV series, the latter a horror movie. Artefacts of popular culture become symbiotic with the protagonists’ lives, mirroring who they are, shaping their futures and becoming spaces to understand themselves in and project themselves into. Manchester-based producer and MC Iceboy Violet’s new album How to Glitch Under the…

quietus.title: The Arrow Storms of Love & Death: Ken Russell’s The Devils
quietus.description: Darran Anderson considers a 'masterpiece' and what it tells us about contemporary power, corruption and lies One sign of a true writer is that there is no event so grim that they cannot convert it into material. In the ruthlessly competitive, sometimes deadly environment of Elizabethan theatre, the playwright Thomas Dekker came in for much derision, though he had moments of inspiration. (If he’s remembered today, it’s for inspiring The Beatles’ ‘Golden Slumbers’ on the Abbey Road medley.) When the Black Death revisited London and the playhouses were shut down, Dekker turned his hand to writing plague pamphlets to survive. They remain valuable records of a cursed time, when social order…

quietus.title: The Body & Cel Genesis – Whole Wide World
quietus.description: The Body & Cel Genesis Whole Wide World The Body's latest collaborative album pairs the duo with Oakland experimental band Cel Genesis for a record of ethereal production and drum'n'bass tendencies Whole Wide World by The Body & Cel Genesis Part metal, part experimental, Whole Wide World is the collaborative work of sludge/metal duo The Body and hardcore gabber group Cel Genesis. Over the years, The Body have been no stranger to expanding their world with avant-garde collaborations, having released the climactic Ascending a Mountain of Heavy Light with Full of Hell in 2017 and Was I Good Enough? with Intensive Care last year, among others. An album two years in the making, Whole Wide World…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Ben Webster :: Music For Loving (1955)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Music for Loving (1955) contains some of Ben Webster’s most sophisticated and elegant work, and the larger arrangements avoid the pitfalls of the “jazz-with-strings” genre. This is none more apparent than when the orchestral bells and whistles step aside, allowing Webster and his band the space to linger in the crestfallen ballads.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Inspiration, Not Limitation :: The Residents’ Eskimo Journey
aquariumdrunkard.description: Many people have seen the Residents, but few know what their members actually look like. The group has maintained anonymity for over 50 years, through hundreds of releases, concerts, books, films, and pretty much every other kind of media. Still, if you've heard of them, you probably know their signature look: tuxedo with top hat perched upon a helmet that resembles a big, veiny eyeball. But did you know the eyeball wasn't always part of the Residents story?

aquariumdrunkard.title: Bob Dylan :: The Rolling Thunder Revue: The 1976 Live Recordings
aquariumdrunkard.description: We all need a hobby. Some people get into fantasy football. Others are obsessed with knitting. There’s cosplay, astronomy, astrology, ham radio … the possibilities are endless. But for my money, the best hobby a guy or gal can have is Bob Dylan. The man just continues to give, even as he cruises through his mid-eighties.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Lotti Tauber :: Concern and Simplicity Volume 1: Original Recordings, 1981–1986
aquariumdrunkard.description: Yet another stunning archival find from the Freedom to Spend label?! Every time this crew pops up, you ask yourself how they’ve somehow unearthed more astounding and unique gems from the past. But FT$ has that magic touch. Case in point: Concern and Simplicity Volume 1: Original Recordings, 1981–1986 , Freedom to Spend’s latest release. Made up of barely circulated material by the late Swiss pianist / composer Lottie Tauber, it’s a minimalist marvel, influenced by Satie, Glass and the I-Ching.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Radio Free Aquarium Drunkard :: November 2026
aquariumdrunkard.description: Freeform transmissions from Radio Free Aquarium Drunkard on dublab. Airing every third Sunday of the month, RFAD on dublab features Tyler Wilcox bringing you two hours of sweet sounds old and new. This month, the first hour is an autumnal selection of classic britfolk instrumental situations. The second hour provides a small/awesome sampling of live performances drawn from the ongoing and immense Aadam Jacobs Archives project. Sunday, 4-6pm PT.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Marshall Crenshaw :: The Aquarium Drunkard Interview
aquariumdrunkard.description: With his crystal clear voice and keen melodic sensibility, Marshall Crenshaw stands as one of the finest rock songwriters going. His latest collection, The Bootleg Sounds of Marshall Crenshaw: 1984-1987 , offers a peek into his process. Culled from his extensive archives, the record brings together unreleased demos, live cuts, and unheard studio recordings captured in the lead up to his third and fourth LPs, 1985's Downtown and 1987's Mary Jean & 9 Others . Full of scuffed up, lo-fi charm, it's a testament to Crenshaw that even his rough drafts feel like brillant slices of pop rock.

aquariumdrunkard.description: In a departure from the usual template of old photos of the artists, the cover of Habibi Funk’s latest reissue features an illustration by Beirut-born, Paris-based artist Raphaelle Macaron. Poolside beach chairs sit empty on the patio of a luxurious apartment complex at dusk, separated by red, rocky terrain from the city skyline in the background. Cool purples, pinks and blues saturate the scene in a clear nod to the style of Hiroshi Nagai, whose work graces the covers of Light in the Attic’s Pacific Breeze City Pop compilations of funk, soul and AOR from 1980’s Japan. But while the references in the album’s title and cover art lovingly highlight the parallels with the City Pop era, the…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Linus + Bonnie ‘Prince’ Billy :: The Outsider: The Music of Jules Decorte
aquariumdrunkard.description: Three oddly-shaped pieces come together in the most natural way in this under-the-radar release from Bonnie ‘Prince’ Billy. The disc reconfigures the work of blind Dutch songwriter Jules de Corte, an outsider artist who wrote and recorded over 3,000 songs during his lifetime. This is not what you’d call a natural fit. De Corte’s songs are quick and witty and cerebral, more like cabaret or art song than BPB’s mournful Americana. Yet the two artists share an unconventional spirituality; there’s real searching in De Corte’s cleverly put together tunes.
